content: Cranberries, particularly in the form of cranberry juice, have been widely used for several decades as a potential method for preventing and treating urinary tract infections (UTIs). The purpose of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness of cranberries in treating UTIs. To conduct this review, a comprehensive search was performed in the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Register of Studies up to August 1, 2023. This database includes studies identified through searches of CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, conference proceedings, the International Clinical Trials Registry Portal (ICTRP), and ClinicalTrials.gov. The search terms used were specifically relevant to the topic of cranberries and UTIs. The review aimed to include all randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or quasi-RCTs that investigated the use of cranberry juice or cranberry products for the treatment of UTIs. Studies involving men, women, or children were eligible for inclusion. Titles and abstracts of potentially relevant studies were screened, and studies that were clearly ineligible were excluded. If a study lacked sufficient information to determine its eligibility, additional details were sought from the authors. Despite this thorough search, no studies were identified that met all the inclusion criteria. Seven studies were excluded because they either used the wrong study design, involved mixed interventions, or failed to report relevant outcomes. One study is ongoing, but its current status is unknown. Based on the findings of this review, no high-quality evidence currently exists to support the effectiveness of cranberry juice or cranberry products for the treatment of UTIs. As a result, there is no reliable evidence to recommend their use for this purpose at this time. The authors emphasize the need for well-designed, parallel-group, double-blind studies to evaluate the effectiveness of cranberry juice and other cranberry products compared to placebo in treating UTIs. These studies should assess outcomes such as symptom reduction, urine sterilization, side effects, and adherence to therapy. Additionally, the appropriate dosage (including the amount and concentration of cranberry products) and the duration of therapy should be carefully evaluated. Both consumers and healthcare providers would benefit from the evidence generated by such rigorous studies.
